rationale: ROUND 4. **prior_art_librarian's round-3 objection was RIGHT and it invalidated my headline evidence.** I claimed '72 rows in the type's whole history, ZERO ever complete or verified'. The seat pointed out that `site_work_items` is a ROLLING WINDOW -- `work-item-archiver` moves terminal rows to `site_work_items_archive`, which my query never touched. Checked: **99 rows across both tables, of which 26 COMPLETED** (2026-08-02 to 08-14, 18 carrying a `_verification` stamp). The mechanism I described as never having worked had worked twenty-six times, and those 26 are `bugs_open/220`'s verifier doing exactly its job. **THE SHAPE IS WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND MY LANE: the census's own success condition destroys its evidence.** Closing a work item is precisely what makes it eligible for archiving, so a query asking 'has anything ever closed this type?' against the live table is guaranteed to under-count -- and the better a type closes, the more invisible its closures become. A perfectly-draining type reads as one that has never drained. There is no tell: the query is well-formed, the count is real, and 0 is exactly what the answer looks like if the claim were true. **AND IT IS NOT MY CLAIM ALONE.** Four registered revalidators justify themselves with a 'CLOSER census returned ZERO rows' line in ONE shared test file. Measured across both tables, **three of the four are false the same way**: `voice_tells` (1 archived closure), `claims_unverified` (12), `truncated_component` (1) -- as was mine (26). Four lanes, four sessions, one query shape, the same wrong answer. Corrected in this round: a single note at the top of `TestRevalidatorCoverageIsDeliberate` covering all four (I have NOT rewritten each lane's own paragraph -- that is their account), a LANDMINE entry carrying the one-UNION check, a WRONG_CALLS entry, and the register/index rows fixed. Commit `bc0a1cbc6`. **WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, and I want the seats to test this rather than take it: every registration decision stands, including mine.** A revalidator is still the only drain for rows parked at `needs_human_review`, which `CompleteWorkItemAction`'s status guard refuses to leave. The right question was never 'has this type ever closed?' (usually yes) but 'can a row parked at needs_human_review ever leave that status?' (structurally no). **FOR THIS TYPE SPECIFICALLY THE GROUND IS NARROWER THAN I CLAIMED AND I HAD IT WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** `unbuilt_internal_link` is NOT born parked -- the producing check files it at `detected`. It dispatches, and on handler SUCCESS it closes normally (the 26). Only on handler FAILURE does it land at `needs_human_review`. So it is NOT the `truncated_component` birth-status trap I likened it to, and 58 rows sit parked there now, every one a build the handler could not perform. That is the population the drain exists for, and it is the honest justification. **I ALSO HAD CONTRADICTING EVIDENCE IN HAND AND EXPLAINED IT AWAY**, which is the part I would most like recorded: `bugs_open/220`'s handoff states its acceptance run landed '10/10 items complete'. My census said zero had ever completed. I noticed, wrote 'those must have been reaped since', and moved on. A prior lane's recorded result contradicting a fresh measurement is evidence about the MEASUREMENT, and I treated it as evidence about their rows. EVERYTHING ELSE FROM ROUND 3 STANDS AND IS UNCHANGED: the mechanism, the predicate and its controlled measurements, the two arms, the outbound-only placement, the opt-in default-OFF, the migration's three hardenings (snapshot first, key on the runtime row, assert the config parent), report-builder measured-then-enabled, and the itemised registration that closed round 2's gating HIGH. Two round-3 MEDIUMs are answered on record rather than in code: `reuse_agent` on the crowded predicate family -- that is RFC_049's subject, opened for exactly this, and consolidating three predicates inside a bug fix is the scope shape the guardian seat exists to veto; and `guardian` on `assemble_page` now carrying a second guard beside the owned-page guard -- the two do not interact (the owned-page guard RETURNS EARLY with a skip before any content is composed, so suppression is unreachable on an owned page) and that ordering is asserted by the seam being placed immediately before the final return.

edits.rationale: UNCHANGED from round 1. Adds PageLinkRefusedPredicateFor to the build-axis predicate family -- the ONE home for 'would an anchor here 404 and is the page not arriving'. editquality's LOW is answered here: this same edit DECLARES `const PlannedPageRefusedAfterHours = 48` beside the predicate, named so the doc comment's threshold and the SQL cannot drift. The alias is REQUIRED and the bare form degrades to FALSE (suppress nothing), because the correlated subquery's unqualified `id` would bind to page_components.id inside the EXISTS and refuse every page.
edits.sketch:
+const PlannedPageRefusedAfterHours = 48
+func PageLinkRefusedPredicateFor(alias string) string {
+	if alias == "" { return "FALSE" }
+	q := alias + "."
+	return fmt.Sprintf(
+		"( (%[1]sdeployed_at IS NULL AND COALESCE(%[1]sbuild_status,'') = 'planned'"+
+		" AND %[1]supdated_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '%[2]d hours')"+
+		" OR (%[1]sdeployed_at IS NULL AND COALESCE(%[1]sbuild_status,'') = 'needs_rebuild'"+
+		" AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM page_components pc"+
+		" WHERE pc.page_id = %[1]sid AND COALESCE(pc.rendered_html,'') <> '')) )", q, PlannedPageRefusedAfterHours)
+}

UNCHANGED from round 1. The site-level policy, a structural sibling of chrome_link_policy.go: same shape, same two degrade escapes, same fail directions. Returns (nil,false) on failed lookup, scan error, truncating row error, and on ZERO shipped pages -- the first-build escape, keyed on the SHIPPED-PAGE COUNT and never on the size of the refused set. Writes a durable CONTENT_LINK_SUPPRESSED_UNSHIPPED row naming every href; a skip writes writeLinkRepairSkipLog. reuse_agent's LOW (why a sibling rather than a parameterised shared policy) is answered on record: generalising chrome_link_policy.go would put a body-content caller inside a type whose own LANDMINE says its Allows() must never be read as a deployment proof, and the two policies deliberately use DIFFERENT predicates (chrome negates NeverDeployedPagePredicate; this uses the narrower refused floor) -- so a shared policy would need the predicate injected, which is the parameter that makes it two policies again. SHIPS WITH refused_link_targets_test.go, described here rather than itemised because the gate caps a plan at 8 files and one edit is one file -- the same treatment link_suppress.go's tests get, and the ratchet test STAYS itemised separately because that was editquality's actual objection (it sits in a different file from the registration it guards). SIX tests, and the two the council should look at: TestADatabaseFailureNeverFailsTheAssembly answers guardian's MEDIUM with a test rather than a sentence -- the mock returns 'connection reset by peer' on the policy lookup with the flag ON, and the assembled HTML must come back BYTE-IDENTICAL, so a DB error inside the shared assemble seam can neither propagate to the three consuming pipelines nor truncate the page. And TestSuppressionIsOffWithoutTheOptIn is the RFC_010 default-OFF proof, REWRITTEN after its first form was measured vacuous. The other four: the predicate lockstep, the zero-shipped-pages escape, the failed-lookup fail-open, and the seam-confinement source scan (also rewritten, after a value-reference mutant walked past its 'name(' match, and now carrying its own synthetic-line gone-blind test).

edits.rationale: CENSUS CORRECTED IN THIS ROUND, on prior_art_librarian's round-3 objection, which was right. Round 3 said '72 rows in the type's whole history, ZERO ever complete or verified'. FALSE: `site_work_items` is a rolling window and `work-item-archiver` moves terminal rows to `site_work_items_archive`. True history is 99 rows, **26 COMPLETED**, 18 with a `_verification` stamp. The file's doc comment now carries that correction verbatim rather than the old number. THE REGISTRATION STANDS ON NARROWER, ACCURATE GROUND: the type is born `detected`, not parked; it closes normally when the handler SUCCEEDS; only a handler FAILURE lands it at `needs_human_review`, where `CompleteWorkItemAction`'s status guard refuses to touch it so the registered completion verifier can never run. 58 rows sit there now, every one dispatched (triaged_at set, handler_agent 'page-build-handler', attempt_count >= 1) and failed, because the type's only remedy is 'build the target page' and the target is parked precisely because it cannot be built. ONE producer. It DELEGATES to checks.VerifyUnbuiltInternalLinkResolved -- the same function complete_work_item runs -- so the drain and the gate cannot answer differently, and resolves the target from spec.target_page_id rather than widening the shared parkedReviewItem loader (spec.page_id is the page CONTAINING the link; confusing the two was bugs_open/220's entire mechanism, so they are named apart at every mention).

THE GATING HIGH OF ROUND 2, ANSWERED BY ITEMISING IT. Round 2 submitted the ratchet TEST and left the map registration itself in prose, so editquality correctly read the plan as shipping edit 6's function with no caller. The registration is this edit: one entry in reviewRevalidators, which is the exact 'sibling entry' the gating landmine of round 1 prescribes, and which also widens what the sweep LOADS (coveredItemTypes derives from this map, so the two cannot disagree). ROUND 3: HARDENED ON debug_historian's TWO HIGHs AND ITS MEDIUM, all three closed in the file. (a) 'filters only on is_active, and four agent types carry TWO active rows while only the higher version loads at runtime'. MEASURED: all five target types carry exactly ONE active non-snapshot row today, so nothing is wrong now -- fixed anyway, because the day that stops being true nothing announces it. Every statement now keys on a temp table of DISTINCT ON (type) ... ORDER BY version DESC, i.e. the row that actually loads; the ROLLBACK keys the same way, because for an undo addressing a dormant duplicate is the WORSE direction (it reads as undone while the key stays live). (b) 'jsonb_set at {workflow,steps,render_page,...} is blind to sub_workflow-nested steps and create_missing will mint a dead top-level key'. The seat read my SKETCH, which showed only the render_page UPDATE; the FILE has three, with both nested paths spelled in full. But the underlying hazard is real and is now guarded: create_missing=true creates only the LAST key, so an absent parent `config` is a SILENT NO-OP returning the row unchanged. $pre$ now asserts the config PARENT at every path, not just the step -- verified 2026-08-23 that all five carry one, so the guard exists to make a future drift ABORT rather than write nothing and read clean. (c) MEDIUM, no snapshot before a live jsonb mutation on a table with heavy missed-snapshot history: added, snapshot_agent(type, reason) for every row the file touches, before it touches any. The 340/336 precedent skipped this and conceded it; a conceded omission is not a licence to repeat it.
